rows.mechanism: region; selector terminal on the left border; tunnels on both borders
rows.evaluation: exactly one case; waits for all inputs; outputs leave together
rows.visible: no — one case at a time; NI's KB says it cannot be done
rows.merge: output tunnel: must be wired in every case or the VI breaks ("Tunnel: missing assignment"); Use Default If Unwired is the discouraged escape
rows.lesson: region is right; the unwired tunnel is Python's may-be-unbound; the two-sided tunnels are why side-by-side cases were declined

rows.mechanism: node with s, t, f inputs
rows.evaluation: both t and f computed (a node needs all inputs)
rows.lesson: this is V4; NI recommends it only when both values are already available, Case when code must not run

rows.mechanism: region; tunnels, auto-indexing tunnels, shift registers, N and i on the border
rows.evaluation: body repeats
rows.lesson: one idiom carries every control construct — Kodosky: the box's boundary 'could hold iteration state information'

rows.mechanism: region with cases stacked above and below
rows.evaluation: one case
rows.lesson: NI staff: it 'works because there's almost always only one wire' and is 'a pain' once tunnels multiply — side-by-side arms are viable exactly when there are no tunnels

rows.mechanism: empirical
rows.lesson: every subject did worse on LabVIEW conditionals than on text; the 'invisible arms' load working memory; users call nested cases spaghetti

rows.mechanism: gate actors: a T-gate/F-gate (switch) per value entering, a controlled merge per value leaving, all driven by one decider
rows.evaluation: only the gated arm receives tokens
rows.merge: controlled merge actor, one per value that leaves; an uncontrolled merge is nondeterministic
rows.lesson: the original one-join-per-leaving-value rule; unrestricted switch/merge makes bounded scheduling undecidable (BDF)

rows.mechanism: φ-function at the join block, one operand per control-flow predecessor
rows.evaluation: 'each execution of a φ-function uses only one of the operands'
rows.lesson: the yield dot is a φ with one operand per arm

rows.tool: Sea of nodes (Click 1995; HotSpot C2, Graal)
rows.mechanism: If node splits control into True/False projections; a Region node merges; Phi nodes hang off the Region with data inputs aligned to its control inputs
rows.evaluation: control token reaches one projection
rows.merge: Phi attached to the Region: 'the PHI nodes at that REGION latch the data value coming from the matching control input'
rows.lesson: V2 literally: the join belongs to the region; V8 later left the IR because effect/control chains made graphs hard to read

rows.mechanism: region nodes group every statement with the same control condition under the predicate's T or F edge
rows.lesson: 'branch as region' formalised in 1987; the arm is the set of statements control-dependent on the test

rows.mechanism: one op with then/else regions; results leave through scf.yield; scf.index_switch for N-way
rows.evaluation: one region runs
rows.visible: yes, both regions in the text
rows.merge: the op's results: 'the types of the yielded values must match the result types'; both regions must yield
rows.lesson: the asymmetry: 'operations inside a region can reference values defined outside of the region' (no input tunnels) but 'a value defined in a region can never be used outside of the region' (yield is the only exit)

rows.mechanism: v1: one Switch per captured tensor and one Merge per output (Dennis-style); v2: a single If op whose branch functions close over inputs
rows.evaluation: untaken arm gets dead tokens (v1); not executed (v2)
rows.merge: Merge per output (v1); the If op's outputs, same number and type per branch (v2)
rows.lesson: an ecosystem that started with token routing moved to the region form, for gradients, XLA and fewer bugs

rows.tool: Simulink If + If Action Subsystem + Merge
rows.mechanism: a port-style If block emits action signals; bodies are conditionally executed subsystems; an explicit Merge block joins
rows.evaluation: only the selected subsystem runs; Switch evaluates both inputs unless 'conditional input branch execution' is on
rows.merge: Merge: 'equal to the most recently computed output of its driving blocks'; signals share memory
rows.lesson: V3's free-standing merge node; a MathWorks engineer prefers If/Merge over Switch: 'I don't like reliance on an optimization to provide good behavior'

rows.mechanism: a composite with one refinement per case, each with its own director
rows.evaluation: one refinement
rows.merge: container ports: 'all refinements have the same ports'
rows.lesson: tunnels by construction; the region's meaning comes from a director, not from the drawing

rows.mechanism: conditional on the method: cases with a control annotation ('if this operation succeeds, go to the next case')
rows.evaluation: one case
rows.lesson: the same one-visible-case cost as LabVIEW, at method level

rows.mechanism: a selector component with ACC and REJ output ports
rows.evaluation: packet routed
rows.merge: none: streams converge on a port
rows.lesson: router-node branching with no join; fine for packets, wrong for a value that must exist once after the if

rows.mechanism: Case with one shared result type for all alternatives; Enso's if_then_else is a lazy method
rows.evaluation: lazy: only the chosen alternative
rows.lesson: an if-expression joins by being a value: V4 is right for `a if c else b`

rows.tool: Blender Geometry Nodes: Switch, Menu Switch, Index Switch
rows.mechanism: select node (N inputs → 1 output)
rows.evaluation: lazy since 3.0: 'only the input that is passed through the node is evaluated'; fields may still evaluate both
rows.visible: yes; Menu Switch hides sockets feeding inactive inputs
rows.lesson: V4's best case; Blender has no conditional zone, so a statement-level if has no home there

rows.mechanism: semantic region with a portless input side and an Output node on the way out
rows.evaluation: body per iteration
rows.lesson: the one live precedent for outside cables reaching straight into a semantic region: 'nodes inside the zone can also take inputs from nodes outside the zone… however, nodes inside the zone can't send their outputs to nodes outside the zone' — the asymmetry, shipped

rows.tool: Houdini: Switch SOP, Switch-If, VOP Switch
rows.mechanism: select node
rows.evaluation: SOPs cook by demand, so only the chosen input cooks; the VOP Switch says the opposite: 'all inputs are evaluated (cooked)'
rows.merge: the node passes one input through unchanged
rows.lesson: laziness is an engine property, not a node property; the same name means both things in one product

rows.mechanism: select node with a 'which' knob
rows.evaluation: pull-based; unused inputs need not be validated
rows.lesson: same as Houdini

rows.mechanism: Branch is an exec pin (True/False pulses); Select is a data node
rows.evaluation: Branch pulses one side; Select evaluates both (UE-20044, open since 2015)
rows.merge: exec wires reconverge on one pin; data rejoined by Select or a variable
rows.lesson: control and data diverge: the pure Select beside the Branch still runs both arms

rows.tool: Unity Visual Scripting; Shader Graph Branch
rows.mechanism: If/Switch on flow; Select and Branch on data
rows.evaluation: flow runs one side; Shader Graph: 'both sides of the branch are evaluated in the shader, and the branch not used is discarded'
rows.lesson: same divergence as Unreal

rows.tool: Max/MSP and Pure Data: gate, switch, select, route, spigot, moses
rows.mechanism: message routers (1→N) and selectors (N→1)
rows.evaluation: lazy by construction: an outlet that does not fire triggers nothing
rows.merge: implicit fan-in, several cords into one inlet
rows.lesson: router branching with no join primitive; the untaken message simply never arrives

rows.mechanism: router: rules → outputs, stop at first match or check all
rows.evaluation: message passing
rows.merge: implicit fan-in, or a join that waits on counts/timeouts
rows.lesson: recombination is where routers hurt: a join waiting on the untaken branch needs a count or a timeout

rows.mechanism: router with labelled true/false handles
rows.evaluation: v1 executes branches in turn; v0 Merge could make both If outputs execute
rows.merge: a Merge node that 'always waits until the data from both inputs is available'
rows.lesson: the v0 bug is the router-plus-merge failure mode in the wild

rows.mechanism: select nodes (Stream Filter, If) and routers (Stream Gate, Dispatch)
rows.evaluation: eager: Grasshopper gates 'leak' (Data Dam is the workaround); Dynamo's If replicates over lists and truncates (issue #6258, open since 2016)
rows.lesson: an eager engine turns a select node into a bug report

rows.mechanism: select node
rows.evaluation: pull system: inactive inputs don't cook unless blending or viewed
rows.lesson: laziness again an engine property

rows.mechanism: an expression inside one node: `if a then b else c` is a line of code
rows.evaluation: lazy method
rows.lesson: dual syntax makes the conditional a node, not a region; no sub-graph bodies

rows.mechanism: router: a Conditional node with true/false output ports; React Flow branches by writing undefined/null to the dead handle
rows.evaluation: packets
rows.lesson: a dead-port convention is what a router needs where a region needs nothing

rows.mechanism: nested blocks / side-by-side columns / flowchart with layout law
rows.evaluation: one body runs
rows.lesson: the readable, structurally scoped references; DRAKON's layout law: main route on the skewer, 'the further to the right, the worse', no crossings
